breaks.quote: If the answer is no, prune. Pick something that still matters to you and prune it.
breaks.why: The reader is told to end something they value, but the reasons (lost hours, a month with no room, the gain of room) were each given a sentence or two inside the writer's own story and never argued in the reader's life, so the case is named, not built.

breaks.quote: I am telling you about my list because I would bet you have one too.
breaks.why: The reader's own case is one short paragraph just before the ask, so the ask rests mainly on the author's single story rather than on the reader's cost.

breaks.quote: Don't wait for it to become useless first, because you may never be able to call any of them useless.
breaks.why: This is the only reason given for acting now and it is one sentence, so the reader is left to guess why this change is worth the loss.
